use_case: AI-enabled device software function (image analysis): estimates respiratory rate from the WM-1 hub's near-infrared camera video when the wearable sensor is off, and flags mismatches when both are available
vendor_or_model: In-house motion-analysis pipeline with a small neural network; runs on the hub (video never leaves the hub)
data_categories: Training: licensed research video of 120 adult volunteers with reference respiratory rate (identifiable; Restricted). Production (planned): chest-region video processed on the hub; only the estimate and a quality score sent to the cloud service
consequential_decision_category: Health care; Safety/CI (device function affecting patient monitoring)
human_in_the_loop: A nurse confirms by manual count before acting; the value is labeled as camera-derived with a quality score; the camera never alarms on its own; the sensor value is primary when attached
applicable_laws: FD&C Act device requirements and 21 CFR 820.10(c) design controls; FD&C Act 524B (cyber device; N31-33-R05); FDA draft guidance on AI-enabled device software functions (notice 2025-01-07, nonbinding); FDA PCCP guidance for AI-enabled device software functions (notice 2024-12-04); 45 CFR 92.210 duties of hospital customers; FTC Act Section 5 (performance claims); dataset license and research consent terms
status: Feasibility; continued work approved with conditions 2026-08-31; not part of the first 510(k)
